Ko decoupling content delivery for medical QA is addressed by DeCode (Decoupling Content and Delivery), which introduces a training-free, model-agnostic framework that adapts existing LLMs to produce contextualized clinical answers by separating “content” from “delivery.” [1] It is designed to handle cases where answers may be clinically correct but not aligned with individual patient contexts, and it evaluates on OpenAI HealthBench. [1]

Related approaches to improving medical QA with external knowledge include RAG-X, which proposes a diagnostic framework to separately evaluate retrieval vs generation in retrieval-augmented medical QA. [7] RAG-X focuses on identifying whether errors come from faulty retrieval or flawed generation, rather than explicitly decoupling content and delivery. [7] Retrieval-augmented systems with grounded evidence are also discussed in a comparative study using fine-tuned open LLMs plus retrieval for factual correctness and reduced hallucinations. [2]
